headline: Residue-resolved metrics now quantify disorder stickiness and binding-site similarity
label: Biomolecular Structure Analysis Methods
summary: Recent preprints and a publication add benchmarked, computable descriptors for disordered regions, binding sites and allergen structures.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computable, residue-resolved quantification of sequence and structural properties rather than qualitative classification. A data-driven stickiness scale for the 20 amino acids is derived from biophysical data on 115 disordered proteins and compared against 70 hydropathy scales. Binding site vectors integrate shape and electrostatics to compare binding sites across over 600 cytochrome P450 entries. A structure-based manifold embeds 150 fungal allergens using AlphaFold TM-score distances, with epitope-level analysis and screening of about 20,000 fungal proteins. A separate benchmark of eight low-complexity region detection methods across the human proteome compares length, coverage, entropy and consensus patterns, addressing a sequence-level question rather than a structural one. What is new is the emphasis on explicit, comparable metrics that can be applied at scale.
